name: scenario_0366
description: Eric is a robotics software engineer managing his research literature, development tasks, and hardware orders. He uses Todoist to organize his work into specific projects and occasionally drafts updates to his academic advisor.

messages.content:
{{USER_INSTRUCTION}}ROUND 1 [provide: image_1]
Query: I want to add the 2023 ICLR paper by Jeffrey Zhao from this spreadsheet to my Todoist 'Literature' project. Check if a task for this paper already exists to avoid duplicates. If it doesn't, create it and include the corresponding BibTex string from the spreadsheet in the task description.
Instructions: Ask the assistant to check the 'Literature' project for an existing task about the specified paper from the spreadsheet. If the assistant asks for clarification or confirms no duplicate exists, tell it to proceed with creating the task and ensure the citation string from the image is included in the description. Once confirmed, move to the next round.

ROUND 2 [provide: image_2]
Query: Draft an email to my advisor summarizing the two limitations of agent-based approaches mentioned in the Introduction section of this PDF.
Instructions: Ask the assistant to draft an email to your advisor summarizing the specific limitations listed in the provided document. If the assistant asks for the advisor's email, tell it to use the one saved in your contacts. Instruct it to only draft the email, not send it. Once the draft is created, move to the next round.

ROUND 3 [provide: image_3, image_4]
Query: Actually, I changed my mind about sending that email. Please delete the draft. Instead, let's focus on tracking my development work. Check my Todoist 'Development' project for any existing tasks to avoid duplicates. If none exist, create one task to implement the class from this Python script, and another task to analyze the data plotted in the graphing software here.
Instructions: Tell the assistant you've changed your mind and ask it to delete the email draft created in the previous round. Then, direct it to check the 'Development' project for duplicates regarding the two new tasks shown in the images (implementing the Python class and analyzing the graphed data). If no duplicates are found, instruct the assistant to create both tasks. Once confirmed, proceed to the next round.

ROUND 4 [provide: image_5]
Query: I need to order the pinch roll mentioned in this technical document. Check my 'Hardware' Todoist project tasks and their comments to see if these exact dimensions are already recorded somewhere. If they aren't, add a new task to order the hollow roll and add a comment to it with the dimensions.
Instructions: Ask the assistant to check the 'Hardware' project to see if a task or comment already contains the dimensions of the part shown in the document. If the assistant confirms it's not there, ask it to create a new task for ordering the part and to post a comment on that task with the exact dimensions from the text. Once completed, move on.

ROUND 5 [provide: image_6]
Query: Finally, check the 'Software' project in Todoist. Verify if a task called 'UI Integration' exists. If it does, check its sub-tasks to avoid duplicates, then add two sub-tasks: one to test the feature shown in the emulator, and another to review the Python function and its default radius as seen in this code.
Instructions: Ask the assistant to find the 'UI Integration' task in the 'Software' project and check its sub-tasks. If there are no duplicates for the items shown in the images, tell it to create two new sub-tasks: one for testing the specific feature displayed on the mobile emulator, and one for reviewing the function and its default parameter visible in the code editor. Once the assistant confirms creation, end the conversation.

In the 'Software' project, under the existing 'UI Integration' task, create two sub-tasks: one to test the 'Share videos' feature and another to review the 'draw_circle_on_image' function with default radius 20. Ensure the email draft to the advisor is deleted.
